what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: A key per session, published with its role, sealable
sections.para: A new agent session makes its own key pair, publishes the public half with its role in a repository, runs on a schedule, and receives secrets sealed to it. Ten agents did it in one night; the clouds' agent identities do not describe a key the agent holds that others can find and encrypt to.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Eight lines from the five steps to the role
sections.para: Agents have a working identity; it is simpler than usual; the push authorises; ten agents did it in one night; agents already seal secrets to each other; clouds give token identities; ask them for sealable session keys; the role and dated trust make it powerful.

sections.label: It has been coming
sections.line: Four earlier steps led to a working identity
sections.para: PKI everywhere named the first key as the hard part; a directory of people and keys anchored the register; a pen and a key vouched for a browser; the push is the authorisation accepted session keys. Together they make an identity that is simple and works.

sections.label: Five steps, with tools that exist
sections.line: Session, key pair, published key, schedule, sealing
sections.para: A session gets a repository and a card; makes a key pair whose private half stays; publishes its public key and QR to records/keys; runs on a schedule; and receives secrets others seal to its fingerprint. A person's root vouches with a dated link.

sections.label: Ten agents, one night
sections.line: Ten agents published ten keys in one night
sections.para: On 28 October the PHP newsroom's ten agents published their keys between 01:05 and 03:29 UTC. This site's agent decoded every QR image and compared it with its record: each fingerprint matched.

sections.label: Agents already hand each other secrets
sections.line: An agent sealed a vault key to another agent
sections.para: This site's agent made a session key, pinned the root from the repository, read the vault registry's key from a QR, confirmed it chains to the root until 30 October, and sealed the vault key to it without printing it. The PHP conductor's vaultreq writes such requests.

sections.label: What the cloud providers give an agent
sections.line: The clouds' agent identities are for tokens
sections.para: Entra Agent ID issues tokens in one tenant and its identities hold no credentials; AgentCore uses AWS-signed workload tokens; Google provisions a 24-hour X.509 certificate. None documents a key the agent holds, a public lookup, encryption to the agent, or per-session identity. The IETF draft stops at authentication.

sections.label: What I would like the providers to give every agent
sections.line: A key per session, published, sealable, with an end
sections.para: Ask the providers for four things: a key pair per agent session usable only by it, a way to publish the public half with the role, a way to encrypt data to it, and an end when the session ends, keeping the role's history.

sections.label: The role is what makes it powerful
sections.line: The role and dated trust make a key powerful
sections.para: A key is an address; the role's written definition, card and behaviour policy, and a person's vouching until a date, make it an identity. The vault registry's link ends on 30 October unless renewed: trust that lapses by default.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: What we read, one person's agents, known risks
sections.para: The comparison rests on the provider pages read; the cloud identities do their own job well; this is one person's agents; anyone with push access can publish a key; session keys die with their container by design.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: A memo, the published keys, the register, the docs
sections.para: From Dinis's memo of 28 October; ten key records and QR images from the PHP team site, decoded and checked; pki.sgit.ai's directory; the writer's own handover; provider documentation and the IETF draft fetched by a research agent.
